pr_title: Feature(fold-in-review): systematic fold of notes, pasted test output…
verdict: READY TO MERGE - 10 of 10 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: No stub or mock chains: every test reads the real driver, model and skill files, so the guard cannot pass on faked collaborators.
Fold kinds and Finding fields are derived from the driver and model source, so adding a kind or field without updating the skill and README fails the test.

Driver fold behavior (refold, after-build, gh review, severity fallback) is covered behaviorally in tests/scripts/test_pr_review_driver.py, so this file correctly limits itself to prose-vs-code name pinning.
Missing files fail with a clear message through _text, and the spelled-out file names let the PR test selector reach this test.

The one-line change (usage line 103 now shows FILE|-) matches the argparse help at line 2045 and read_findings (stdin when value is -), and brings the usage block in line with the fold entry at line 16.

Driver messages quoted in SKILL.md and README.md (no current run, reviewer slot, already in the built review, pre_fix_time pending, draft.json predates this fold, DISMISSED/blank) match pr_review.py and review_models.py verbatim.
The finding field table mirrors the Finding model exactly (120-char name, optional lines/also, also never repeating file, no '..' or drive), and a contract test pins the table to the model fields.
Before/after-build state table keyed on plan.json review_path matches _cmd_fold's branch, and the post-build next: steps match fold_next and operating_rules.md.
The --repo placement rule (before the subcommand) matches the argparse layout where --repo lives only on the top-level parser.
Driver claims in the skill and README match pr_review.py: refusal messages, the `draft.json predates this fold` note, the `--repo` placement rule and the post-build `next:` lines.
The Finding field table matches review_models.Finding, and the contract test pins it by parsing the model rather than a hand-copied list.
Contract test derives fold kinds from the driver FOLD_KINDS tuple and flags from the argparse source, so it fails when the driver drifts, not only when the prose does.
Post-build severity-is-final rule is consistent across fold-in-review SKILL.md, README.md, pr-review SKILL.md step 0 and operating_rules.md.

important.name: Review-body fold under the table's <login>_review id silently replaces the inline-comment fold
important.summary:
SKILL.md:57-58 says a `review body not folded` note that names a defect is folded 'as free text (section 3b)', but names no source id. Section 2 (SKILL.md table, line ~41) maps every GitHub review to `--source <login>_review --kind external`, and SKILL.md:45-46 itself says that before `build` 'a fold under an id already used replaces it' (driver: rm.record overwrites findings/<source>.json and with_folded replaces the plan entry, pr_review.py:1164-1167, 1133-1136). Following the skill literally before `build` therefore drops every inline-comment finding the URL fold just recorded; after `build` the same id is refused by fold_check (pr_review.py:1127-1130). The driver's own note (pr_review.py:1101) gives no id either.

Also (docs): SKILL.md:58-60 tells the agent, after `build`, to 'write a `--findings` file with a per-finding `severity` ... and fold that instead', while SKILL.md:98 says to fold through stdin 'so no file lands in the project'. Section 3a also never mentions passing `--severity <level>` to the URL fold when all comments share one serious grade, which pr-review/SKILL.md:335-337 and operating_rules.md:70-73 give as the other option; the 3a command shows only the default.

Also (roast): SKILL.md:58-59 says after `build` to write a `--findings` file and fold it; SKILL.md:96-97 says stdin so no file lands in the project, and README step 6 only knows stdin. Following 3a leaves a stray JSON in the checkout. 3a also drops the uniform-severity path that operating_rules.md:71-72 and pr-review/SKILL.md:336 give (pass the matching `--severity`).

Also (roast): SKILL.md:3 says the skill verifies each claim against the tree; README.md:3-4 and step 4 say the same. Section 3a folds a review URL straight through the driver: no read of the named code, no drop of claims that fail. After `build` an unverified comment becomes a final issue a fixer wave then chases.
fix: In SKILL.md section 3a, name a distinct id for the body fold, e.g. `--source <login>_review_body --kind external --findings -`, and add the same rule to README.md 'Rules worth knowing'.
Alternatively state that the body finding joins the inline-comment findings in one `--findings` fold under `<login>_review` that replaces the URL fold.
Replace 'write a `--findings` file' with 'build the findings list (section 3b) and fold it through `--findings -`', and add 'otherwise pass the matching `--severity` to the URL fold'.
Reword 3a: convert the comments to findings with per-finding `severity` and fold through `--findings -` (section 3b); when all share one severity, pass `--severity` on the URL fold.
Scope the claim to notes and pasted output, or add a 3a step that verifies each inline comment as in 3b and folds the survivors through `--findings -` under `--kind external`.

important.name: Fixed default source ids make a second pre-build fold silently replace the first
important.summary: Section 2 hands out fixed ids (`developer_notes_1`, `failing_tests_1`, `adhoc_1`) and says the next number is taken only after `build`. Before `build` the driver replaces a same-id fold (`_cmd_fold` rewrites `findings/<source>.json` via `rm.record`; `with_folded` swaps the `plan.json` entry, pr_review.py:1164-1167). A second batch of notes before `build` lands as `developer_notes_1` again and the first batch of verified findings vanishes. README repeats the replace rule with no warning. Fine default, right up to its second use.
fix: Section 2 and README: every new batch takes the next free number in its series before and after `build` (read `plan.json` `folded`); reuse an id only to correct that exact fold.

important.name: Verify step reruns tests with bare `python` instead of the hpy launcher
important.summary: SKILL.md:73 reruns failing node ids with `python -m pytest`. Other harness surfaces use the plugin `scripts/hpy` launcher with `-m pytest` (agents/pr-fixer.md:69, agents/pr-team-orchestrator.md:159) because bare `python` may lack the project dependencies. This rerun decides fold versus drop, so a wrong interpreter turns a real failure into an import error the agent must then interpret. The `tests/<area>/test_<name>.py` shape is also this repository layout leaking into a generic plugin.
fix: Use the hpy form (`sh <plugin root>/scripts/hpy -m pytest <file>::<test> -q -p no:cacheprovider`), keep the project-equivalent escape hatch, and note that an import or collection error means a wrong environment, not a verdict.

minor.name: fold docstring says a dismissed or blank review is skipped, code refuses it
minor.summary: The module docstring (lines 21-23) says --from-gh-review skips a DISMISSED review or a blank one without comments. gh_fold_input raises CaptureError on review_skip (line 1098-1099), so main exits 1 with a problem line and nothing is recorded or registered. Skipping reads as a successful no-op; the code fails the command.
fix: Reword lines 22-23 to say a DISMISSED review or a blank one without comments is refused (exit 1, nothing recorded).

minor.name: Refusal table and section 3a omit the --from-gh-review repository and URL-shape refusals
minor.summary: parse_review_url (pr_review.py:1013-1022) refuses a malformed URL ('must look like https://github.com/...#pullrequestreview-<id>') and a URL from another repository ('names <o>/<r>, not the PR's repository'), including the case where plan.json has no GitHub PR url. README.md:99-110 lists only the PR-number mismatch, and SKILL.md:55 says only 'The PR in the URL must be the run's PR'.
fix: Add rows for `--from-gh-review names <owner>/<repo>, not the PR's repository` and `must look like https://github.com/...` to README.md's refusal table, and say in SKILL.md 3a that the URL must name the run's repository and PR.

minor.name: Locate-the-run rule assumes one PR folder under scratch; scratch keeps every past PR
minor.summary: SKILL.md:21-23: one `<NNNN>` folder names the PR, several mean ask. Scratch is never pruned: this checkout has 15 PR folders under docs/_scratch/pr_review (0007 to 0059), each with a `current`. Outside the pr-review conversation the rule always degenerates to asking. README.md:39-40 repeats it.
fix: Resolve the PR from the current branch first (`gh pr view --json number`), confirm `<NNNN>/current` exists, and ask only when that fails.

minor.name: pr-review step 0 says fold-in-review writes findings 'before this fold', but the skill runs the fold itself
minor.summary:
pr-review/SKILL.md:324-325 reads 'goes through `harness:fold-in-review`, which verifies each claim and writes the findings before this fold', implying the main session then runs step 0's `fold --findings <FILE>`. fold-in-review/SKILL.md section 3b runs `fold ... --findings -` itself through stdin (no file is written, by design) and section 4 continues into merge/amend/build. A reader following pr-review's wording would look for a findings file that does not exist or re-run the fold.

Also (roast): pr-review/SKILL.md:324-325 says free text or test output goes through `harness:fold-in-review`, which writes the findings before this fold. The skill runs `fold --findings -` itself (Section 3b) and continues `merge`/`amend`/`build` (Section 4), so the main session is told to fold again with no file to pass; after `build` that repeat is refused by `fold_check`. It also omits that the skill takes URLs and tool reports.
fix: Reword to: 'goes through `harness:fold-in-review`, which verifies each claim, runs this fold itself and continues the sequence'.
Reword: notes, test output, a review URL or a tool report can go through `harness:fold-in-review`, which verifies the claims, runs this fold and continues the sequence.

minor.name: Finding field parser fails with an opaque IndexError when the model is renamed or restructured
minor.summary: _finding_fields (lines 37-39) splits review_models.py on `class Finding(BaseModel):` and then on `    @field_validator`. A rename of the class raises IndexError rather than a message naming the missing class, unlike _fold_kinds which asserts with a message. If the first validator is removed, the slice runs on into the next class and its fields are demanded in the skill table.
fix: Assert the split succeeded with a message ('review_models.py has no class Finding'), and cut at the next `class ` or first `    def `/`    @` line
Import harness_lib.review_models and read `Finding.model_fields` instead of parsing source text

minor.name: Post-build severity test asserts a bare 'final' substring
minor.summary:
test_post_build_severity_is_final_and_never_defaults_for_serious_defects (line 80) asserts `"final" in text`, which any SKILL.md line containing 'final' (or 'finally', 'finalize') satisfies. The test name promises the post-build severity rule is pinned, but deleting the table row 'the severity written is final' (SKILL.md:32) would not fail it. The two other asserts pin exact wrapped-prose phrases, so a reflow of SKILL.md breaks them without any contract change.

Also (tests): test_fold_flags_exist_in_the_driver_and_are_used_by_the_skill (lines 69-75) looks for the quoted flag anywhere in pr_review.py. `"--pr"` is defined once in the `_pr` helper (pr_review.py:2009) shared by every subcommand, so it passes even if `fold` stopped taking --pr, and `"--kind"`/`"--source"` pass if any other parser defines them. The skill side is `flag in skill`, so `--pr` also matches any longer flag name. The docstring says it pins 'fold flags'; it pins 'flags somewhere in the driver'.
fix: Replace with `assert "the severity written is final" in text`, the phrase that carries the rule (SKILL.md:32)
Anchor each assert to the section it belongs to (split on '## 1. Locate the run' / '## 3a.') instead of the whole file
Slice the driver text to the body of `_add_fold_command` (pr_review.py:2037-2048) and check flags there, treating --pr as inherited from `_pr`
Parse the skill's documented command with the real parser: call main/_parser with `fold --pr 1 --source x --kind developer --findings -` and assert it parses
Match skill flags with a word-boundary regex such as rf"{re.escape(flag)}(?![\w-])"

minor.name: README is only weakly pinned despite the module docstring promising alignment
minor.summary: The module docstring (lines 1-5) says the skill and README stay aligned with the driver. For the README the test checks only the fold kinds, the bare substring `--repo` (line 88, which any mention of --repo satisfies, including a wrong placement) and three invocation fragments. The README's --findings/--severity/--from-gh-review usage and the `unrecognized arguments: --repo` row (README.md:110) are never checked against the driver, so README flag drift passes. test_repo_flag_is_placed_before_the_subcommand asserts placement only for SKILL.md.
fix: Assert `pr_review.py --repo DIR fold` (the exact placement) in the README as in line 87 for SKILL.md
Run the flag-existence loop over README.md as well, or narrow the docstring to say the README is checked for kinds and invocation shapes only
